gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a grid-tied balcony battery stops sending power through the wall plug the moment the grid fails, or that EcoFlow's own US STREAM page restricts its sale and plug-and-play installation to Utah. EcoFlow says the system 'immediately ceases grid-tied output' in an outage and that 'backup power is reserved solely for essential appliances,' meaning the devices plugged into its two NEMA 5-15/5-20 outlets. The page lists only UL 1741 and IEEE 1547, not the UL plug-in PV certification that California's SB 868 requires.
standout_why: I compared three cited pages. californiabalconysolar.com/sb-868 quotes the law's text: UL plug-in PV certification and a feature that isolates the device so it can't backfeed in an outage. pluginsolartracker.com/california says kits need 'certified protection against feeding the grid in an outage.' KQED says current products 'do not yet meet the outlined requirements.' None of them says what that means for a battery system: the house circuits go dark in an outage and only the battery's own outlets stay live. None names the UL 3700 standard. None mentions that EcoFlow's US STREAM, the $1,399 card ChatGPT showed, is sold only for Utah and claims UL 1741 and IEEE 1547 rather than plug-in PV certification. None says that no battery-backed plug-in system is UL 3700 listed. The one 'first UL 3700' product, Hoymiles HiFlow Pro, is a microinverter with no battery, and its 'certified' claim is itself disputed.
decides: This removes the EcoFlow STREAM from consideration for a California shopper today. EcoFlow sells it only for Utah. From Jan 1, 2027, SB 868 requires UL certification as a plug-in PV system, and EcoFlow's US page doesn't claim that. If the shopper wants outage backup, anti-islanding means a grid-tied balcony battery can't run the apartment's wall circuits during a blackout either way. A portable power station charged by its own panels does the same job without connecting to the grid: an Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 bundle, EcoFlow DELTA 3, BLUETTI AC180 or Elite 200 V2 solar kit, or ALLPOWERS P1800 plus SP037. Load-shifting to lower the bill is the only reason to choose a grid-tied unit, and in California that has to wait for a UL 3700-certified product.

findings.label: Outage behaviour (anti-islanding)
findings.value: "In the event of a power outage or abnormal grid disconnection, the system immediately ceases grid-tied output"
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System (EcoFlow US)
findings.note: The maker's US product page. The fetch tool cut the quote at 125 characters. The sentence goes on to say this keeps grid-tied operation secure.

findings.label: What gets power in an outage
findings.value: "In an outage, backup power is reserved solely for essential appliances"; 2 AC outlets, NEMA 5-15/NEMA 5-20

findings.note: The page lists no wattage for off-grid use of those outlets. It gives only on-grid output (next finding).

findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System (EcoFlow US)
findings.note: 1,200 W matches SB 868's per-dwelling cap of 1,200 W AC.

findings.label: California law: outage isolation and certification
findings.value: Device must have a feature that 'isolates the portable solar generation device from the building's electrical system' to prevent 'backfeeding electricity to the electrical grid during a power outage', must be 'certified as a plug-in photovoltaic system by Underwriters Laboratories', and is capped at 1,200 W AC per dwelling through a receptacle
findings.source_title: SB 868: The Plug Into the Sun Act | California Balcony Solar
findings.note: §8530(c)(1), (2), (5) and (6) as quoted on that page. A cited rival already has this; I list it for context.

findings.label: UL plug-in PV standard
findings.value: UL 3700, 'the Outline of Investigation for Interactive Plug-In Photovoltaic Equipment and Systems'. It covers construction, performance and labeling, including protection 'against overloads and prevent electric current from flowing in the wrong direction'
findings.source_title: UL Solutions debuts testing and certification framework for safer plug-in solar across the United States
findings.note: UL press release dated 2026-01-08. Batteries and energy storage aren't mentioned.

findings.label: UL 3700 and battery systems
findings.value: Jason Szumlanski (Florida Solar Design Group): UL 3700 requires plug prongs to de-energize in under 1 second after disconnection, requires anti-islanding and ground-fault protection independent of the receptacle GFCI, and 'does not contemplate' battery systems; Clause 1.8 limits scope to circuits where every component is listed for bidirectional current flow
findings.source_title: Plug-In Solar Is Here, and It Was Never Designed for Your Battery System
findings.note: This is the author's description of the standard, dated 2026-07-26. I couldn't open the standard's own text.

findings.label: First UL 3700 plug-in microinverter (no battery)
findings.value: Launched 2026-07-15; 'first North American safety standard specifically designed for plug-in photovoltaic systems'; up to four units on separate sockets, 1,200 W total; no battery or storage mentioned
findings.source_title: Hoymiles Introduces HiFlow Pro, the First UL 3700-Compliant Plug-in Microinverter in the US to Boost DIY Solar
findings.note: Hoymiles' own word is 'compliant'. A search snippet reports pv magazine USA and InsideEVs saying it isn't UL-certified, but I didn't open those pages, so I don't rely on that.
